Progress payments are not the default, though: performance-based payments are the preferred financing method when practical and the contractor agrees, and in DoD they must be conditioned on the achievement of performance outcomes, never on costs incurred.

cite.quote: The customary progress payment rates for DoD contracts, including contracts that contain foreign military sales (FMS) requirements, are 80 percent for large business concerns and 90 percent for small business concerns.

unlimited.q: When does the Government get unlimited rights in technical data?
unlimited.a: When the item, component, or process was or will be developed exclusively with Government funds — plus categories like form, fit, and function data; data necessary for installation, operation, maintenance, or training purposes other than detailed manufacturing or process data (that OMIT carve-out is the most-fought-over line in DoD data rights — dropping it flips the answer); and publicly available data.

cite.quote: The Government obtains unlimited rights in technical data, computer software, or computer software documentation that are— (1) Technical data related to an item, component, or process which has been or will be developed exclusively with Government funds; (2) Studies, analyses, test data, or similar data produced in the performance of a contract when the study, analysis, test, or similar work was specified as an element of performance; (3) Created exclusively with Government funds in the performance of a contract that does not require the development, manufacture, construction, or production of items, components, or processes; (4) Form, fit, and function data; (5) Necessary for installation, operation, maintenance, or training purposes (other than detailed manufacturing or process data);

unlimited.q: Mixed Government and private funding produced the technical data. What rights arise, and for how long?
unlimited.a: Government purpose rights. The period is negotiable with a five-year period nominal, and it begins upon execution of the contract, subcontract, or similar instrument that required the development — not at delivery. When it expires the Government's rights become unlimited, including the right to authorize others to use the data or software for commercial purposes.

cite.quote: The period during which government purpose rights are effective is negotiable. A five year period is nominal. Either the Government or the contractor may request a different period. (3) The government purpose rights period begins upon execution of the contract, subcontract, or similar contractual instrument that required the development. Upon expiration of the Government rights period, the Government has unlimited rights in the data or software including the right to authorize others to use the data or software for commercial purposes.

unlimited.q: Development was exclusively at private expense. What rights does the Government get in the technical data versus the noncommercial software?
unlimited.a: Limited rights in the technical data; restricted rights in the noncommercial computer software. Limited rights data cannot be used, released, or disclosed outside the Government without the asserting contractor's permission — except when necessary for emergency repair and overhaul, to a covered Government support contractor, or to a foreign government (other than detailed manufacturing or process data) for evaluational or informational purposes in the interest of the United States.

cite.quote: Do not use, release, or disclose data in which the Government has limited rights outside the Government without the permission of the contractor asserting the restriction except when it is— (i) Necessary for emergency repair and overhaul; (ii) To a covered Government support contractor; or (iii) To a foreign government, other than detailed manufacturing or process data, when use, release, or disclosure is in the interest of the United States and is required for evaluational or informational purposes.

unlimited.q: Delivered technical data arrives marked with restrictive legends the program doubts. What is the Government's recourse, and how long does it have?
unlimited.a: A contractor's assertions do not, by themselves, determine the Government's rights. Review asserted restrictions before accepting the deliverable, and the contracting officer may challenge an assertion when reasonable grounds exist to believe it is invalid — within six years after final payment or six years after delivery of the data or software, whichever is later. Commercial products and services are presumed developed exclusively at private expense whether or not the contractor submits a justification, so challenging one takes specifically stated reasonable grounds — and on that commercial presumption a failure to respond to the challenge notice cannot be the sole basis for a final decision denying the restriction.

cite.quote: Challenge assertions within six years after final payment under the contract or six years after delivery of the data or software, whichever is later.

unlimited.q: A contractor helped write the work statement for a competitive services acquisition. May it compete to perform the services?
unlimited.a: Not generally. A contractor that prepares or assists in preparing the work statement may not supply the system or services unless it is the sole source, it participated in the development and design work, or more than one contractor was involved in preparing the work statement.

cite.quote: that contractor may not supply the system, major components of the system, or the services unless— (i) It is the sole source; (ii) It has participated in the development and design work; or (iii) More than one contractor has been involved in preparing the work statement.

unlimited.q: How long does the contracting officer have to issue a final decision on a certified claim over $100,000?
unlimited.a: 60 days after receiving the certified claim — or, within those 60 days, notify the contractor of the time within which a decision will be issued. One senior-level escape hatch: if a claim over $100,000 carries a defective certification, the contracting officer has no obligation to render a final decision at all, provided the contractor is notified in writing, within 60 days of receiving the claim, of the reasons the attempted certification was found defective.

cite.quote: For claims over $100,000, 60 days after receiving a certified claim; provided, however, that if a decision will not be issued within 60 days, the contracting officer must notify the contractor, within that period, of the time within which a decision will be issued.

unlimited.q: The contracting officer never issues a decision within the required time. What happens to the claim?
unlimited.a: The failure is deemed a decision denying the claim, and it authorizes the contractor to file an appeal or suit.

cite.quote: Any failure of the contracting officer to issue a decision within the required time periods will be deemed a decision by the contracting officer denying the claim and will authorize the contractor to file an appeal or suit on the claim.

unlimited.q: The Government terminates a contract for convenience. How does the contractor get paid, and on what clock?
unlimited.a: Through settlement with the termination contracting officer. The final settlement proposal is due within one year of the termination date unless the TCO allows more time, and it covers all cost elements including subcontract settlements and proposed profit. The TCO negotiates a fair and prompt settlement where possible, settling by determination only when agreement fails; a no-cost settlement closes it out when no costs were incurred or the contractor waives them and nothing is owed the Government. Partial payments may flow before settlement when the contract authorizes them. And if a default termination is later found improper or excusable, the parties' rights and obligations convert to those of a convenience termination.

cite.quote: The final settlement proposal must be submitted within one year from the termination date, unless the TCO allows more time.

unlimited.q: Transfers of Government contracts are statutorily prohibited. When does recognizing a successor in interest require a novation agreement — and when is a novation unnecessary?
unlimited.a: A novation is the vehicle when it is in the Government's interest and the third party's interest arises from the transfer of all the contractor's assets, or the entire portion involved in performing the contract. It is unnecessary for a change in ownership by stock purchase with no legal change in the contracting party, where that party remains in control of the assets and keeps performing — the ownership changed, the contractor did not. A name-only change with rights and obligations unaffected takes a change-of-name agreement instead.

cite.quote: A novation agreement is unnecessary when there is a change in the ownership of a contractor as a result of a stock purchase, with no legal change in the contracting party, and when that contracting party remains in control of the assets and is the party performing the contract.

unlimited.q: Suspension of work versus a stop-work order — which contracts, and what happens to profit?
unlimited.a: A suspension of work applies to construction and architect-engineer contracts; if unreasonable, the contractor may claim increased costs of performance excluding profit. Stop-work orders are for negotiated fixed-price or cost-reimbursement supply, R&D, and service contracts, require approval above the contracting officer, and are never a substitute for a termination notice.

cite.quote: A suspension of work under a construction or architect-engineer contract may be ordered by the contracting officer for a reasonable period of time. If the suspension is unreasonable, the contractor may submit a written claim for increases in the cost of performance, excluding profit.

unlimited.q: A final determination disapproves one of a contractor's business systems. Which systems are covered, and what happens to the contractor's payments?
unlimited.a: Six systems: accounting, earned value management, estimating, material management and accounting, property management, and purchasing. On a final determination with a notice to withhold, the contracting officer withholds 5 percent from progress payments and performance-based payments and directs a 5 percent withhold on interim cost vouchers until all material weaknesses are corrected. An acceptable corrective action plan submitted within 45 days and effectively implemented drops the withhold to 2 percent. Ceilings: 5 percent for material weaknesses in any single system, 10 percent across multiple systems.

cite.quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold 5 percent of amounts due from progress payments and performance-based payments, and direct the Contractor, in writing, to withhold 5 percent from its billings on interim cost vouchers on cost-reimbursement, labor-hour, and time-and-materials contracts

unlimited.q: Are liquidated damages a penalty for late delivery?
unlimited.a: No. They are not punitive and not negative performance incentives — the rate must be a reasonable forecast of just compensation for the harm caused by late delivery or untimely performance, used when timely performance is critical and actual damage would be hard to prove. For DoD construction the liquidated-damages clause (52.211-12) is mandatory in every contract exceeding $900,000 — except cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts or where the contractor cannot control the pace of the work — and optional at or below that figure.

cite.quote: Liquidated damages are not punitive and are not negative performance incentives (see 16.403-2). Liquidated damages are used to compensate the Government for probable damages. Therefore, the liquidated damages rate must be a reasonable forecast of just compensation for the harm that is caused by late delivery or untimely performance of the particular contract.

unlimited.q: Under which contract types is the contractor generally not held liable for loss of Government property?
unlimited.a: Cost-reimbursement, time-and-material, labor-hour, and fixed-price contracts awarded on the basis of certified cost or pricing data. DoD extends the shield to negotiated fixed-price contracts awarded on a basis other than certified cost or pricing data — so in DoD practice the carve-out reaches essentially every negotiated fixed-price award, leaving sealed-bid fixed-price as the main place full liability survives.

cite.quote: Generally, contractors are not held liable for loss of Government property under the following types of contracts: (1) Cost-reimbursement contracts. (2) Time-and-material contracts. (3) Labor-hour contracts. (4) Fixed-price contracts awarded on the basis of submission of certified cost or pricing data.

unlimited.q: On a small business set-aside for services, how much may the prime pay to subcontractors that are not similarly situated?
unlimited.a: No more than 50 percent of the amount the Government pays for contract performance. The limit is also 50 percent for supplies (excluding materials), 85 percent for general construction, and 75 percent for special trade construction.

cite.quote: Services (except construction), it will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities.

unlimited.q: What two-part test makes a manufactured end product "domestic" under the Buy American statute?
unlimited.a: The article must be manufactured in the United States, and the cost of domestic components must exceed the applicable content threshold — 60 percent, rising to 65 percent for 2024-2028 deliveries and 75 percent from 2029 (with a separate less-than-5-percent foreign iron and steel rule for predominantly iron or steel products). Per 41 U.S.C. 1907 the domestic content test is waived for COTS items — though not for the iron/steel test, except COTS fasteners. For DoD, the content test counts U.S. and qualifying country components toward the threshold.

cite.quote: The article must be manufactured in the United States; and (2) (i) Except for an end product that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both, the cost of domestic components must exceed 60 percent of the cost of all the components, except that the percentage is 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029. But see paragraph (d) of this section. In accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1907, this domestic content test of the Buy American statute has been waived for acquisitions of COTS items (but see paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section).

unlimited.q: What does the Berry Amendment restrict DoD from buying unless it is domestic?
unlimited.a: Items such as food, clothing, tents, cotton and other natural fiber products, wool, canvas products, and hand or measuring tools — they must have been grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States unless an exception applies.

cite.quote: do not acquire— (1) Any of the following items, either as end products or components, unless the items have been grown, reprocessed, reused, or produced in the United States: (i) Food.

unlimited.q: In an acquisition covered by the WTO Government Procurement Agreement, what end products may be acquired?
unlimited.a: Only U.S.-made or designated country end products (or U.S. or designated country services), unless offers for them are not received or are insufficient to fulfill the requirements. DoD narrows the field twice: trade agreements apply only to end products in the product service groups enumerated at 225.401-70 — if the end product is not in a listed group, the trade agreements do not apply — and in covered acquisitions DoD buys only U.S.-made, qualifying country, or designated country end products unless such offers are not received or are insufficient, or a national interest waiver is granted.

cite.quote: in acquisitions covered by the WTO GPA, acquire only U.S.-made or designated country end products or U.S. or designated country services, unless offers for such end products or services are either not received or are insufficient to fulfill the requirements.

unlimited.q: What contract types must be used for awards resulting from a commercial solutions opening?
unlimited.a: Fixed-price type contracts, including fixed-price incentive. A CSO is a general solicitation for innovative commercial products or services under 10 U.S.C. 3458, and what it buys is treated as commercial.

cite.quote: Notwithstanding FAR 12.104, contracting officers must use fixed-price type contracts, including fixed-price incentive contracts, for awards resulting from a CSO.

unlimited.q: How can a follow-on production contract from an other-transaction prototype project skip a new competition?
unlimited.a: It is excepted from the competition requirements when the OT agreement for the prototype, awarded under 10 U.S.C. 4022, included provisions for a follow-on production contract and the statutory conditions are documented.

cite.quote: Also excepted from this part are follow-on production contracts for products developed pursuant to the “other transactions” authority of 10 U.S.C. 4022 for prototype projects

unlimited.q: When is an Earned Value Management System required?
unlimited.a: The civilian baseline is major acquisitions for development, per OMB Circular A-11. DoD replaces that wholesale with thresholds: on cost or incentive contracts, EIA-748 compliance is required at $50 million or more, and at $100 million or more the contractor must have a system the cognizant Federal agency has validated against EIA-748. Below $50 million, applying EVM is optional and a risk-based decision; on firm-fixed-price contracts of any value it is discouraged (waiver procedures apply); and the subpart does not apply to contracts primarily for software.

cite.quote: In accordance with OMB Circular A-11, agencies must require an Earned Value Management System (EVMS) in major acquisitions for development.
